(a) In General.—Subchapter I of chapter 449 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:“§ 44927. Expedited screening for severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans“(a) Passenger Screening.—The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans, shall develop and implement a process to support and facilitate the ease of travel and to the extent possible provide expedited passenger screening services for severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans through passenger screening. The process shall be designed to offer the individual private screening to the maximum extent practicable.“(b) Operations Center.—As part of the process under subsection (a), the Assistant Secretary shall maintain an operations center to provide support and facilitate the movement of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans through passenger screening prior to boarding a passenger aircraft operated by an air carrier or foreign air carrier in air transportation or intrastate air transportation.“(c) Protocols.—The Assistant Secretary shall—“(1) establish and publish protocols, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and the organizations identified under subsection (a), under which a severely injured or disabled member of the Armed 
Forces or severely injured or disabled veteran, or the family member or other representative of such member or veteran, may contact the operations center maintained under subsection (b) and request the expedited passenger screening services described in subsection (a) for that member or veteran; and“(2) upon receipt of a request under paragraph (1), require the operations center to notify the appropriate Federal Security Director of the request for expedited passenger screening services, as described in subsection (a), for that member or veteran.“(d) Training.—The Assistant Secretary shall integrate training on the protocols established under subsection (c) into the training provided to all employees who will regularly provide the passenger screening services described in subsection (a).“(e) Rule of Construction.—Nothing in this section shall affect the authority of the Assistant Secretary to require additional screening of a severely injured or disabled member of the Armed Forces, a severely injured or disabled veteran, or their accompanying family members or nonmedical attendants, if intelligence, law enforcement, or other information indicates that additional screening is necessary.“(f) Report.—Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, and annually thereafter, the Assistant Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the implementation of this section. Each report shall include each of the following:“(1) Information on the training provided under subsection (d).“(2) Information on the consultations between the Assistant Secretary and the organizations identified under subsection (a).“(3) The number of people who accessed the operations center during the period covered by the report.“(4) Such other information as the Assistant Secretary determines is appropriate.”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of subchapter I of chapter 449 of title 49, United States 
Code, is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 44926 the following new item:


“44927. 
Expedited screening for severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only intra-government coordination (TSA with the Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs) plus a report to Congress, neither of which counts. But the Assistant Secretary must also consult outside advocacy organizations for severely injured or disabled service members and veterans, both when developing the screening process and when establishing the protocols. Those organizations are non-federal parties consulted before a federal decision, so this is participation.
fable.s: The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans, shall develop and implement a process

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Assistant Secretary to consult with 'organizations... that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans' before developing and implementing a process for expedited screening. These advocacy organizations are outside the federal government, satisfying the definition of participation. While the section also involves consultation with federal Secretaries (which is not participation), the inclusion of outside advocacy groups makes the overall requirement one of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans, shall develop and implement a process...

opus.w: The Assistant Secretary must consult outside advocacy organizations for injured or disabled service members and veterans before developing the expedited screening process and its protocols. That is consultation across the federal boundary before a federal decision. The consultation with the Defense and VA Secretaries, and the annual report to Congress, are intra-government and would not count alone. But naming non-federal advocacy organizations makes this participation.
opus.s: The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans, shall develop and implement a process
opus.b: **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** Most of the consultation here is between federal officials (the TSA Assistant Secretary, the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs), and the report goes to Congress. Both of those stay inside the federal government. That reading misses that the same consultation also includes advocacy organizations, which are outside the government. The statute requires consulting them before developing the screening process and before setting its protocols.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Assistant Secretary to consult with outside advocacy organizations (non-federal entities) when developing and implementing the expedited screening process. While consultation with other Secretaries is intra-governmental, the inclusion of outside advocacy organizations in the consultation requirement constitutes participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members of the Armed Forces and severely injured or disabled veterans, shall develop and implement a process
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: The section mentions "organizations identified by the Secretaries... that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members," which might suggest outside participation. However, the definition states that consultation between federal agencies (Secretary of Defense, Secretary of Veterans Affairs) is intra-governmental and thus "No." The key is whether the *organizations* are involved in the decision-making process. The text says the Assistant Secretary shall develop the process "in consultation with... organizations identified by the Secretaries... that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members." These advocacy organizations are outside the federal government (non-profits, etc.). Therefore, the federal government must consult with outside entities before making the decision to develop/implement the process.

Wait, let's re-read carefully. "The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and organizations identified by the Secretaries of Defense and Veteran Affairs that advocate on behalf of severely injured or disabled members... shall develop and implement a process..."

The "organizations" are outside the federal government. The Assistant Secretary (federal) must consult with them. This fits the definition: "consultation or coordination with... non-profit organizations... before making a decision." The decision is the development and implementation of the expedited screening process.

Therefore, the label is Yes.
